criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p xtask`. A new test builds the homepage from a fixture job's records and asserts the rendered HTML contains that job's id, its producer model, a different verifier model, the verdict, and a recorded cost for each stage, with a link to the source record.
criteria.evidence: I ran the test `site::evidence_tests::the_homepage_shows_a_jobs_models_verdict_and_stage_costs_from_its_records` and it passed. It builds a fixture records branch in a temp git repo with RecordsWriter: two readings, a verification record, and two invocations costing $1.25 and $0.75. It renders the study page with the section added. `shows_job_evidence` then checks the section for the job id, both models, `pass`, $1.25, $0.75, `/blob/` and `/records/jobs/2026-10/` links, and at least 3 links. It also checks that the newest reading is the one shown and that the section comes right after ``.

criteria.criterion: A new test calls the same check on a page rendered with the section removed, or with the job's records missing, and asserts the check fails (the page does not pass). Run `cargo test -p xtask` to see it pass.
criteria.evidence: I ran `a_page_without_the_section_or_without_the_records_fails_the_check` and it passed. It asserts that `shows_job_evidence` fails on three pages: one without the section, one built from a repo with no records branch (that page says 'could not be read here'), and one for a job id the branch does not hold.

criteria.criterion: `git diff` shows the section's values (models, verdict, costs) are computed from record data in site.rs code and not typed into string literals. The diff contains no hand-written model names or dollar figures outside test fixtures.
criteria.evidence: In the diff, `read_evidence` reads `producer_model` and `verifier_model` from the newest reading-N.json, `final_verdict` and `agent_verdict` from verification.json, and role, model and cost.value from invocations/*.json. It reads them through `ls_tree_under` and `cat_blob` at the records tip. The only hand-written value outside the tests is the job id `EVIDENCE_JOB = "20261029-073603-7kqv"`. Model names and dollar figures appear only in the `evidence_tests` fixtures. I checked the evidence snapshot: this job is landed (outcome.json state "landed"), its reading-1.json has producer_model claude-sonnet-5-5 and verifier_model claude-opus-5-5, its verification.json has final_verdict "pass" at the top level, and all 7 invocations have top-level role, model and cost.value.

criteria.criterion: `git diff` touches only xtask/src/site.rs (plus xtask files the section strictly needs). The header text, the existing sections' text and the CSS are unchanged, and the only change to `render` is one call that places the new section.
criteria.evidence: Files changed: CHANGELOG.md, xtask/src/decisions.rs and xtask/src/site.rs, all on the expected list. In decisions.rs, the branch-tip lookup is moved out of `locate` into `records_tip`, and `locate` behaves as before. The CSS, the header and the other section functions are unchanged. `render` is not changed at all. Instead `build` wraps its output in `with_evidence(...)`, a single placement step that puts the section directly under the header. That meets the intent (one placement, nothing else changes) but not the exact wording (see the minor finding).

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test`. All pass, including every pre-existing site.rs test.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for f8daefb7 (CI run 42861581062) show fmt, clippy and test all passed. I also ran `cargo run -q -p xtask -- site` in the snapshot and it wrote index.html and decisions.html without error. The output is outside my working directory, so policy did not let me read it.

criteria.criterion: Outcome check: the producer model and verifier model in the rendered section differ from each other, so the page backs the claim that a different model checks the work. This is asserted in the test.
criteria.evidence: The page prints 'a different model checked it' only when the two models it read differ (`evidence_html` compares them). `shows_job_evidence` requires that phrase, and the test also has `assert_ne!(PRODUCER, VERIFIER)`. For the real job the snapshot shows claude-sonnet-5-5 as producer and claude-opus-5-5 as verifier, so they differ.

findings.summary: No test runs `build()` and checks that the section is in the output, so if the `with_evidence` call were dropped from `build`, no test would fail.
findings.evidence: Both new tests put the page together themselves with `with_evidence(study_page(), &evidence_section(...))`. The existing `build_writes_index_html_at_the_output_root` test does not look for `job-evidence`. If that call were removed, clippy's dead-code warning under -D warnings would probably still catch it, but a direct test of `build()` against a fixture records branch would cover the request's 'rebuilt without that section' more exactly.

findings.summary: Records are read as untyped serde_json values with hand-written field names, although xtask already depends on athena-data and the accepted reading said to use its record types.
findings.evidence: The code reads `producer_model`, `final_verdict` and `cost.value` with `Value::get`. xtask/Cargo.toml already lists `athena-data.workspace = true`, and the reading's assumption said to parse with AnyRecord and check_record_file. If a field is renamed, the typed structs would fail to compile, but this code only fails at page-build time and then quietly shows the 'could not be read' section.

findings.summary: The section is placed by replacing the first `</header>` text in `build()`, not by a call in `render` as the reading planned.
findings.evidence: `html.replacen("</header>", ...)` works today because `render` writes exactly one header and writes it first. Passing the section into `render`, or having `render` call it, would not depend on the HTML text.

findings.summary: If the records branch cannot be read when the site is published, the live page shows a 'could not be read' note and the build still succeeds.
findings.evidence: pages.yml fetches the records branch with `|| echo ::warning::`, so a failed fetch only logs a warning. The section then says no values are shown, which is honest, but on the published page it means the header claims are again unsupported until someone notices.

summary: The change does what was asked. The homepage now has a section titled "Check it on a real job", placed directly under the header. It names job 20261029-073603-7kqv and shows the producer model, the verifier model, the verdict, and a table with each stage's model, recorded cost and a link to the source record. All of these values are read from the job's records on the records branch when the page is built; none are typed into the code. I checked that job in the evidence snapshot: its outcome record says it landed, and the fields the code reads are all there. They give producer claude-sonnet-5-5, verifier claude-opus-5-5, verdict pass, and seven stages with recorded costs that add up to the $4.97 in outcome.json. I could not show those real values on a rendered page, because this snapshot has no records branch. The pages workflow does fetch that branch before building the site. The two new tests pass when run with `cargo test -p xtask evidence_tests`. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test runs passed. The header, the existing sections and the CSS are unchanged. The diff touches only files on the expected list. Four minor findings, none blocking: (1) no test runs `build()` itself and checks for the section; (2) the records are read as untyped JSON rather than through the typed athena-data structs; (3) the section is placed by replacing the first `</header>` text in `build()` instead of by a call in `render`; (4) if the records branch can't be read, the published page silently shows a "could not be read" note instead of failing the build.
